newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Burns Philp seen set for flat result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Burns Philp seen set for flat result.

text.p: Global food ingredients group Burns, Philp and Co Ltd is expected to report on Thursday a fairly flat pre-abnormal net profit for the first half to end-December, share analysts said on Wednesday.
The market is expecting a result near the A$52.5 million net profit reported for the corresponding half last year, with few surprises.
"They've still got to pay a lot of slotting costs this half," said a Sydney-based food analyst, referring to the costs of gaining supermarket shelf space in the competitive U.S. spice market.
"It also reflects a fairly lacklustre performance in their other markets," the analyst said. "The Australian yeast market is pretty bad and the European businesses aren't exactly firing."

The spices and yeast manufacturer, which has operations in Australia, the United States, Asia and Europe, suffered in 1995/96 ended June 30 due to a stronger Australian dollar and higher raw material prices.
Burns Philp recorded a net loss for the year of A$61.8 million following an abnormal loss after tax of A$136.6 million.
Managing director Ian Clack said after November's annual general meeting that raw material costs were falling, while slotting fees were abating.
Burns Philp reported a net profit for the first quarter of 1996/97 of A$17.6 million, up A$5.2 million from the same period a year earlier.
Total sales for the quarter declined six percent, but sales from ongoing businesses were seven percent higher in local currency terms, a trend which was likely to persist, said one analyst.
The company's share price has fallen from a recent high of A$2.49 in January to A$2.23 at Tuesday's close, but remains well above last year's closing low of A$1.60 in September.

Queried in mid-January by the Australian Stock Exchange about the fall in its share price, Burns Philp said it had no explanation, and confirmed that first half operating profit before abnormals and tax would not vary by more than 15 percent.
It was also unaware of anything that might require the recording of a material abnormal result.

Burns Philp did not pay a final 1995/96 dividend, but told shareholders at the annual meeting it hoped to pay a first half dividend this year comparable with the eight cents paid in the first half of 1995/96.
